segments.t: Amid the noisy buzz of ASK's anniversary celebration, Mathias learns alarming news about his star client Guillaume Canet. Andrea urgently pulls him aside into a quiet room to discuss the impending crisis without alerting the party. Listen to the scene in French first.
Tais-toi, ne parle pas ici!
Pourquoi me tires-tu le bras ainsi?
Il y a un très gros problème.
Qu'est-ce qui se passe encore?
Guillaume Canet ne viendra pas ce soir.
Je sais, il tourne en Ukraine.
Non, il veut quitter notre agence!
Mais d'où tiens-tu cette folie?
J'ai d'excellentes sources bien informées.
Guillaume est mon client le plus fidèle.
Une agence rivale lui fait les yeux doux.
C'est un véritable coup de poignard!
Viens, il faut qu'on parle discrètement.
Allons tout de suite dans mon bureau.
Let's walk through the conversation step by step.
Tais-toi, ne parle pas ici!
'Be quiet, do not speak here!' Andrea hushes Mathias in the middle of the party. The imperative verb warns him to maintain secrecy.
Pourquoi me tires-tu le bras ainsi?
'Why are you pulling my arm like that?' Mathias wonders why she is acting so frantically. The interrogative sentence reflects annoyance.
Il y a un très gros problème.
'There is a very big problem.' Andrea delivers a grave warning about agency stability. The short sentence signals impending danger.
Qu'est-ce qui se passe encore?
'What is going on now?' Mathias asks what latest catastrophe has hit ASK. The informal phrase conveys mounting exhaustion.
Guillaume Canet ne viendra pas ce soir.
'Guillaume Canet will not come tonight.' She reveals the unexpected absence of their star client. The future negation raises an alarm.
Je sais, il tourne en Ukraine.
'I know, he is filming in Ukraine.' Mathias tries to brush aside her worry with an alibi. The present tense provides a harmless excuse.
Non, il veut quitter notre agence!
'No, he wants to leave our agency!' Andrea drops the bombshell regarding his client's departure. The exclamation reveals devastating news.
Mais d'où tiens-tu cette folie?
'Where do you get this madness?' Mathias refuses to believe the shocking rumor. The interrogative phrase questions her intelligence.
J'ai d'excellentes sources bien informées.
'I have excellent, well-informed sources.' She insists her insider information is solid. The noun phrase defends her credibility.
Guillaume est mon client le plus fidèle.
'Guillaume is my most loyal client.' Mathias proudly defends his special bond with the actor. The superlative adjective expresses trust.
Une agence rivale lui fait les yeux doux.
'A rival agency is courting him.' Andrea warns that competitors are circling their top talent. The idiom describes aggressive poaching.
C'est un véritable coup de poignard!
'That is a real stab in the back!' Mathias reacts with outrage at the prospect of betrayal. The dramatic metaphor highlights the stakes.
Viens, il faut qu'on parle discrètement.
'Come, we must speak discreetly.' Andrea pulls him away from listening ears. The imperative verb initiates a confidential retreat.
Allons tout de suite dans mon bureau.

'Let us go to my office right away.' Mathias agrees to plan their defense in private. The adverbial phrase emphasizes urgency. Now listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.

Threatened with the loss of their top star, Andrea and Mathias unite to protect ASK from outside predators. Listen to the conversation once more in French.
Nous devons sauver ce contrat capital.
